title: Global target transport through the composition comparison
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ and $h:X'\to X$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes, $Z'=Z\times_X X'$, $j:Z'\to X'$ and $p:Z'\to Z$ its projections, and $F$ an etale sheaf of sets. Let $t$ be a global section of $i^*F$, presented on the base change of the identity object of $X$. Use the actual constructions of [def-weil-pbc-gabber-h0-zariski-constructions]. For the chosen unit-compatible composition isomorphism $c:h^*F\mapsto j^*h^*F\cong (h\circ j)^*F$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], its component on the top-open etale object sends the constructed target section $t_H$ to the section comparison of $t$ along $p$, restricted along the canonical top-open-to-identity-pullback isomorphism. The comparison is [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison] for the triangle $Z'\xrightarrow{p}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$ with composite identified with $h\circ j$ by the fibre-product equation. No representative, local open, closed-immersion or finite-morphism hypothesis is required. The scheme fibre product, etale sheaf and etale morphism notions are those of [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets, def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: Factor the defining global-section isomorphism into the top-open identification, the composition comparison, the pullback-pasting isomorphism and equality transport. Naturality of the composition comparison moves the top-open identification through it. The resulting map to the identity pullback is canonical, by cancellation of its second projection, which is an isomorphism.

Cancel the inverse global-section isomorphism. Identify the remaining equality transport with section comparison along the first projection by equality elimination. Restrict the resulting composite section along the top-to-identity-pullback isomorphism. These are identities of section functions and apply also to empty schemes.
